intro.text: Two well-known agile methods: Extreme Programming, called X P, and Scrum.

weekly.text: X P works in weekly cycles. On the first day, the customer picks the stories for that week. By the end of the week, there are running, tested features. A quarterly cycle is a release.

tdd.text: X P writes the test first. Write a failing test. Run it and watch it fail. Write code until it passes. Run it again. Repeat. That is test-driven development.

pair.text: All production code is pair programmed. The driver types. The navigator reviews every line.

more.text: Code is integrated many times a day, anyone may change any code, and the pace is sustainable: a forty-hour week.

scrum.text: Scrum starts with a backlog: the customer's wants and needs, each one a user story.

sprint.text: A sprint is a thirty-day cycle. It takes a set of stories from the backlog.

daily.text: Every day, the scrum master runs the daily scrum. No more than fifteen minutes.

team.text: A scrum team has no more than six to nine members.

demo.text: At the end of the sprint, the team shows the customer a demonstration of working, integrated, tested software.
